assumption: Writers and tools will converge on a shared front matter vocabulary drawn from RSS 2.0 (title, author, pubDate, description, source, enclosure) plus urlPrev, urlNext, image, inlineImage and metaImage, so acting on those names reaches most Markdown-web content.
evidence: INT-001 asks for it explicitly and cites overlap with Jekyll, Hugo, Eleventy, Astro and Obsidian. Only one corpus (scripting.com) uses it today, and the vocabulary is undocumented.
test_method: Survey front matter keys in the markdownWeb archive, Andrew Shell's site and a sample of Jekyll/Hugo/Obsidian repos; track whether other Markdown-web browsers adopt the names.
